briefs.rationale: Rewrote the contours-and-cauchy brief so it still covers the contour-Goursat-Cauchy arc to analyticity, residues and zero-pole counting, the Poisson-Dirichlet-Hartogs-pseudoconvexity-Runge-Mittag-Leffler-Gamma-Weierstrass control of boundary values, approximation, principal parts and special functions, the Montel-Schwarz-Pick-Bloch-Schottky-Picard-Riemann-mapping conformal side, and the simply connected and analytic-continuation globalisation through periods, primitives, harmonic conjugates and monodromy, and now also covers the four gained pages: Green kernels and harmonic measure with conformal covariance, the Poisson-Jensen route to Nevanlinna's first main theorem and order of growth, Cauchy-Pompeiu and Bochner-Martinelli solutions of the d-bar equation giving Dolbeault vanishing and Hartogs extension, and Riemann surfaces with branched maps, genus and Riemann-Hurwitz, with the zeta page still applying the machinery to Euler products, continuation and the functional equation.

Rewrote the foundations brief so it still covers the Banach-space, Fourier, Hahn-Banach and duality, weak-topology, Schauder-basis, Bochner-integration and Radon-Nikodym spine, Hilbert geometry, orthonormal bases, compact-operator and Fredholm theory, Banach algebras and operator calculi, Gelfand theory, the compact self-adjoint spectral theorem with Hilbert-Schmidt kernels and trace-class operators, Frechet calculus and Stone's theorem, and now also covers the two gained pages: Fredholm determinants and Lidskii's trace formula for trace-class operators, and measurable Hilbert fields with direct integrals and the spectral multiplicity model for separable abelian von Neumann algebras.

Rewrote the homotopy-and-covering-spaces brief so it still covers homotopy, the fundamental group, unique lifting, the conjugacy-class classification of connected coverings, regular coverings and deck groups, the circle cover and its subgroups, Seifert-van Kampen pushouts with the sphere, wedge, product and torus consequences, and the retract, Borsuk-Ulam, topological-group and punctured-space obstructions, and now also covers the gained page: triangulation and polygon moves give every nonempty compact connected surface a normal form, with orientability and Euler characteristic (2-2g, 2-k) as the complete invariant. The brief states the nonempty hypothesis; the Axiom of Choice the classification theorem assumes is carried by the statement itself, as in the rest of this brief.
